entries.message: Fix - Stop resume positions discarding library caches, and version assets per build
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Fix: Stop resume positions discarding library caches, and version assets per build

Fix: Saving a resume position no longer throws away the cached history, movies, shows and stats data, none of which depends on it; with a dashboard open during playback that was spending 22% of the time rebuilding on a normal library and 47% on a very large one, and is now zero
Fix: Open pages still see resume progress move, because the change signal the browser watches now covers both watch history and resume positions
Fix: Marking something watched still refreshes every derived view exactly as before
Fix: Each build now serves its own asset URLs, so pulling a new build no longer leaves the browser running the previous build's JavaScript from cache

majorBugFixes: Stop resume positions discarding library caches, and version assets per build

Marking something watched still refreshes every derived view exactly as before
Each build now serves its own asset URLs, so pulling a new build no longer leaves the browser running the previous build's JavaScript from cache

entries.message: Fix - Make the media and library pages substantially faster
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Fix: Make the media and library pages substantially faster
Fix: TV shows whose episodes all fall outside the most recent 25,000 watches no longer disappear from the TV Shows library; on a 90,000 watch test library that restored 408 missing shows

Fix: Opening a TV show or episode page no longer makes an external metadata request just to look up an id the app already stored, and no longer re-asks Plex, Emby and Jellyfin whether the title is available on every single load
Fix: An episode page asked the server for the same show record four times and now asks once, cutting about 1.1 seconds and 84KB from the load

Fix: Movie and show pages no longer carry streaming availability for every country in the world when only two are shown, taking a movie page's metadata from 100KB to 76KB and the stored metadata here from 105MB to 63MB
Fix: Movies pages answer from a cached projection instead of re-deriving the whole library each time: pages 1, 5 and 10 went from about 60ms to under 1ms on a 90,000 row library

Fix: Library pages load all of a screen's posters in one request rather than one per card, and adding another page of results now appends the new cards instead of rebuilding every card already on screen
Fix: The Stats page no longer downloads every period's report to display one, and the restore screen no longer re-downloads the whole restore report on every poll
Fix: Library reads are backed by new database indexes, taking season lookups from 798ms to 28ms and recent-order reads from 767ms to 48ms

The Stats page no longer downloads every period's report to display one, and the restore screen no longer re-downloads the whole restore report on every poll
Library reads are backed by new database indexes, taking season lookups from 798ms to 28ms and recent-order reads from 767ms to 48ms

entries.message: This update includes resolve code scanning alerts (#27), close remaining stack trace exposure (#28), and cut the cost of the Movies, Stats and restore screens.
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Tweak: This update includes resolve code scanning alerts (#27), close remaining stack trace exposure (#28), and cut the cost of the Movies, Stats and restore screens.
Tweak: Keep stack traces out of admin-visible diagnostics and harden provider parsing and logging against CodeQL findings.
Tweak: Normalize caught provider, credential, outbound, and watchlist errors before they can reach API responses.

Tweak: Movies pages now answer from a cached projection instead of re-deriving the whole library on every request: pages 1, 5 and 10 went from about 60ms to under 1ms on a 90,000-row library, and the page number no longer changes the cost

Tweak: The Stats page no longer downloads every period's report just to display one; it receives the totals, a short list of the available years and months, and only the report being viewed, fetching a different period when you pick one

Tweak: A completed restore's full result and log are stored separately from the live status row, so the restore screen stops re-downloading the entire report on every poll while still showing the whole log
Tweak: Library reads are backed by new database indexes covering season and title lookups, provider ids and recent ordering, with planner statistics refreshed once after they are created
Tweak: Poster and backdrop paths are stored as their own columns on the metadata cache, so artwork no longer requires parsing the full details blob
Tweak: Versioned assets are now cached for a year while the app entry page and manifest keep revalidating, so a new release is still picked up immediately

entries.message: This update includes sync up next and watched state across providers and prevent stale media renders and harden sync performance.
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Tweak: This update includes sync up next and watched state across providers and prevent stale media renders and harden sync performance.

Tweak: Keep Up Next and watched state aligned across Plex, Emby, and Jellyfin, repair newly available provider episodes, preserve accurate progress, restore episode titles, and polish refresh/menu controls.
Tweak: Prevent stale media detail responses from repainting the dashboard after rapid navigation.
Tweak: Keep show and movie detail hydration, watch actions, and provider-derived state consistent during asynchronous loads.
Tweak: Improve scheduler, live-session, and incremental provider-sync behavior for reliable updates.
Tweak: Bound and instrument derived-cache rebuilds and add repeatable large-library performance baselines.
Tweak: Harden response caching, compression, and asset-version handling for safer browser loads.
